subject: Acme Health — incident notification scope & evidence cooperation
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-12-19T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Security inquiry — timeline + evidence for recent service degradation

Hi Marissa,

We saw an elevated error rate affecting our workloads yesterday evening that correlated with a Redwood service incident. Our security and compliance teams are preparing an evidence request to satisfy internal auditors and a couple of regulators. I attached Acme's standard evidence request (Acme_evidence_request_v2.pdf) — can you confirm which of the requested artifacts you can provide and your expected timelines?

Key asks:
- Initial incident notification window and what fields you include (scope, affected tenants, suspected root cause)
- Whether Redwood can provide log slices / request IDs tied to our tenant and approximate delivery timeline
- Which subprocessors (if any) were involved in the affected call path; we may need proof of subprocessor notification or any mitigations they performed
- Any cross-border transfer approvals needed before we can receive exported data

Please send a short mutual action plan so our security team can track commitments. If you prefer, loop in your legal/privacy folks.

Thanks,
Samantha Li
Sr. Security Program Manager
Acme Health

Attachment: Acme_evidence_request_v2.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-19T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Security inquiry — timeline + evidence for recent service degradation

Samantha — thank you for the packet and the clear asks. We're opening a dedicated track internally and will provide a short mutual action plan below.

Quick summary (high level):
- Initial notification: we will provide a preliminary incident notice within 72 hours of triage completion (aiming for <48 hours where possible) that includes scope (affected model routes/tenants), estimated timeframe, and immediate mitigations.
- Evidence handoff: we can deliver redacted request IDs, aggregated KPIs, and a curated log slice tied to Acme's tenant within 5 business days subject to legal review; full raw dumps require an executed data transfer addendum if cross-border exports are involved.
- Subprocessors: we'll confirm whether any third-party processing (CDN, observability, storage) was in the call path and provide confirmation of subprocessor notifications within the same evidence window.
- Cooperation: Redwood will assign a single technical liaison and a legal contact for evidence transfer; we can use an SFTP share or secure Drive link depending on the item class.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) 0-24h: Acknowledgement and point-of-contact (this email).
2) 24-72h: Preliminary notice with scope and interim mitigations.
3) 3-7 business days: Curated evidence package (redacted logs, request IDs, timeline spreadsheet).
4) 7-15 business days: Root-cause analysis and full remediation summary.

Please confirm whether the MAP timelines meet Acme's compliance windows. Ben / Lauren / Neha — tagging you for legal/privacy and commercial alignment. I'll prepare the notify matrix and share a short timeline spreadsheet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (will attach redwood-notify-matrix.xlsx after alignment)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-19T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Acme evidence & contract levers

Looping quickly — Acme is asking for fairly quick artifacts. A few commercial/legal points to check:
- Contractually, DPA says 72-hour notification but doesn't mandate raw log exports; we should confirm whether to offer a time-limited escrow of logs as a commercial accommodation.
- If subprocessor evidence requires disclosure beyond the DPA, procurement may push for a limited redline to the subprocessors clause.
- Price/credits ask: historically customers request small goodwill credits in exchange for expedited exports. Do we want to pre-authorize a credit?

Neha — can you confirm our SOC2 scope and whether the storage/CDN provider was in the path for this incident? Lauren — any objections to committing to a curated package in 5 business days and a fuller RCA in 10?

—Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-12-19T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Security inquiry — timeline + evidence for recent service degradation

Thanks Marissa — that MAP looks workable. A couple of clarifications before we lock timelines:
- Our internal compliance rule: initial notice within 72 hours is required for our regulators. If you can commit to "prelim within 48h" that's preferred.
- Regarding subprocessors: we need confirmation that no cross-border subprocessor exported Acme customer payloads (even temporarily). If a subprocessor was involved, we need (a) confirmation they were notified, (b) a short summary of their remediation steps, and (c) whether they performed any export of tenant data.
- For evidence transfer: redacted logs are fine; however our legal team may request a secure transfer for certain IDs (DocuSign preferred).

If Redwood can commit to the MAP with the 48h preliminary window and 5 business day curated package, we'll mark this as aligned and proceed to coordinate the data transfer method.

Regards,
Samantha

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmehealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-20T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Security inquiry — timeline + evidence for recent service degradation

Samantha — thank you and apologies for the back-and-forth. From a legal/privacy perspective here's our formal position and commitments under the existing DPA, plus a narrow accommodation to help you meet your audit window: 

1) Notification windows: Redwood's DPA requires us to notify customers of confirmed incidents without undue delay and to provide a preliminary notice as soon as practicable. Practically, our internal SLA is to issue a preliminary notice within 72 hours; for this event we will aim to deliver a preliminary notice within 48 hours and will escalate internally to meet that timeframe.

2) Evidence & scope: We will provide a curated evidence package (redacted logs, request IDs, timeline spreadsheet, and a short runbook of mitigation steps) within 5 business days. We cannot provide unrestricted raw log exports without an executed data transfer agreement if the export includes personal data crossing jurisdictions. Where redaction still meets your audit needs, we will deliver those artifacts expeditiously.

3) Subprocessors: We confirm we are performing an internal mapping now to identify any subprocessors in the affected path. If a subprocessor was involved and performed processing of Acme tenant payloads, Redwood will: 
   - Provide confirmation that the subprocessor was notified;
   - Provide a short summary of any remediation steps they took;
   - Provide any evidence of data export activity (e.g., transfer logs) to the extent the subprocessor permits disclosure under their contracts.

4) Cross-border transfers: If certain artifacts require cross-border transfer approvals, we will propose a limited data transfer addendum that narrows scope to the specific evidence set and limits retention. If acceptable, we can fast-track that addendum and deliver a DocuSign link for signature.

5) Cooperation & liaison: Redwood will provide: 
   - Technical liaison: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com) for log correlation and dataset delivery;
   - Legal/privacy liaison: Neha Kapoor (neha_kapoor@redwood.com) for DPA/addendum questions.

6) Commercial accommodations: Any credit or goodwill for expedited handling will require a quick commercial approval; Ben, please propose a cap for expedited exports.

I'll attach the notify matrix and a suggested DocuSign addendum draft for a limited transfer. If Acme confirms the MAP with 48h preliminary notice and the 5 business day curated package, we'll begin the evidence pull today.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-notify-matrix.xlsx, RDWD-DTA-exhibit-draft.docx
